history.p: During his stay in Rome in 1833, Hans Christian Andersen was inspired by reading Rahbek's and Nyerup's edition of the old heroic ballads to write an opera text about Hr. Sverkel, however he had to give up his original idea that the music should be arrangements of the old folk songs. The text underwent several changes before Andersen handed it over to Hartmann in 1844, after Ivar Bredal had declined to arrange the music.The original intention was that it should be a Singspiel with spoken dialogue, but eventually it turned into a one act opera with recitatives. According to the newspaper reviews the premiere in May 1846 was a success, but Hartmann was not entirely happy with Sverkel's romance, so at his suggestion Andersen wrote a new text, which became No. 7, the recitative and romance "Ja, jeg er hjemme / Langt, langt fra Hjemmets Kyst", which was used for the first time on 4 March 1847, and from then on has been one of the most loved numbers in the opera. Apparently the opera was not very popular until the revival during the 1858/59 season, when it was advertised as "an original romantic opera in two acts". Thereafter it became extremely popular, especially after the war with Prussia and Austria in 1864 when it became a kind of national opera, passing its 100th performance in 1891. When it was performed at the celebration of Hartmann's 150th birthday 14 May 1955, it reached its 312th performance.

physDesc.physMedium: Written in black ink. Paper 18 and 20 staves. A few additions by Hartmann in ink (different colour from the original) and a few later corrections in pencil in an unknown hand. End-dating: "I:P:E: Hartmann d. 21 Marts [in a different hand] 1846"..

annot.p: The first title page, "Liden Kirsten / romantisk Synge Stykke / i én Act / af H.C Andersen", originally functioned as title page for the copy of the autograph of Act One, of which only the overture is now preserved, and which along with the autograph score of Act Two made up the earliest complete edition of the opera. This volume was long thought lost, but was transferred to the Royal Library in 1997 in connection with the purchase by the Cultural Heritage Committee of Wilhelm Hansen Publishers' archives. The autograph score served as printing manuscript for the edition of Wilhelm Hansen's. (Plate no. 13717) published in 1905.

physDesc.condition: The manuscript has severe marks of fire. It was completely restored in 2003, when it was separated from the rest of the volume.

physDesc.physMedium: In brown half-binding with title on spine in gold. Pages have been trimmed in connection with the binding, which carries the monogram of Frederik IX, indicating that the earliest possible date of the binding is 1947. The copy shows signs of frequent use. Written in brown ink. Paper: 18 staves, except insertion pp. 47-50: 16 staves; insertion pp. 81-84: 12 staves; insert pp. 197-200: 16 staves. Numerous additions in pencil, ink and blue brown crayon. Various earlier paginations in pencil and ink, beginning on p. 3, thus disregarding the insertion on pp. 1-2. From p. 35 (no. 8) to the end of the volume all bifilios are numbered in ink as "39-80"; no bifolio numbering on pp. 1-34 (No. 7) because of the insertion with the new version of No. 7, dated a month and a half later than the end-dating of the whole. End-datings: "I:P:E: Hartmann 28 Decbr 1846" (p. 21, end of No. 7); "23/4 45." (p. 35, beginning of No. 8); "25/4 45." (p. 46, end of no. 8); "I:P:E: Hartmann d: 10 Novbr: 1845 Op: 44" (p. 218, end of Act Two).

In full cloth binding with handwritten label in Hartmann's hand pasted on front cove,r inscribed: "Liden Kirsten / Text af H.C. Andersen / Claveerudtog. / Op: 44. / 1846." Written in black ink. Paper: 18 staves. Two first pages blank and unpaginated, from first music page paginated 1-98. Pages. 1-8 (overture), pp. 1-98 (Nos. 1-10). Between pp. 2 and 3 of the overture a bifolio has been inserted with 8 bars "ad pag 2 più facile" (simplified version of bb. 72-79 of the overture). Page 6 contains an alternative, simplified version (più facile). Overture dated on page 8: "I:P:E: Hartmann d: 20 Septbr. 1846". At the end of the music on p. 98 signed and end-dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann Op. 44 / Strandveien 8 Septbr 1846".

annot.p: Comments on pages 9 and 30 suggests that the autograph was used as the printing manuscript for the piano score, issued by the publishers C.C. Lose & Delbanco in November 1846.

annot.p: Liden Kirsten (2); Mor Ingeborg (2); Fru Malfred (2); Etle (2); Sverkel (1); Narren (1); vl.1 (5); vl.2 (4); va. (3); vc. (3)., cb. (3); fl. (3); ob. (2), cl. (2), fg. (2), cor. (3); tr. (2); trb. (3), timp., arpa. S.1 (6); S.2 (5); T.I, (2); T.2 (2); B.1 (3); B.2 (3). The parts were used at the first performance on 12 May 1846 and apparently were employed for all 332 performances at The Royal Theatre. Ongoing changes have been added in the course of time including musicians' handwritten signatures from performances right up to 1947, as well as a performance in Stockholm in 1928. The material bears strong traces of having been used many times. The instrumental parts in faded purple cardboard with cloth spines, the choral parts in blue cardboard.

physDesc.physMedium: Written in ink with corrections and cancellations in pencil. Unsigned and undated; inserted in blue board and inscribed: "Liden Kirsten / 71 B / [in an different hand] 71 A." Notated for 2 violins, used for rehearsing the dances in Nos. 2, 6, 9, and 12. Originally drawn up for the performance in 1846 by the same copyist who wrote out the parts. Later additions in French about the choreography of August Bournonville, probably used in connection with his rehearsal of the opera on 29 October 1858. A number of figures added in Bournonville's hand probably refer to the now lost overview with the notations of the dances in connection with the revival on 24 April 1869.

annot.p: Material for the performance in Weimar, January 1856. Dating in the prompt score: 17 January and 1 February. Overture with revised ending. No. 7: the original version followed by the altered one in both score and parts (including Hialmar's part) with neither of the versions cancelled. After the first version Hartmann has given a reference to the second version by adding "siehe Pag. 165"; before the second version in Hartmann's hand: "Der nächststehende Recitativ mit Romance kann statt der Arioso benutzt werden." Contrary to the rest of the score, the whole of the new version of no. 7 is written in Hartmann's hand. No. 12: Fru Ingeborg's lines in the original version with introductory speech without music. Names of characters: Frau Malte, Ingeborg, Etla, Karin, Hialmar, Narr. Numerous remarks in German in the score in Hartmann's hand.

annot.p: Manuscript copy with a number of corrections and additions by Andersen; handed in by Andersen to The Royal Theatre on 5 October 1844. The wavy lines in various places in the text, mentioned on the title pages, mean that Andersen originally meant the work to have interpolated spoken dialogue; thus the original genre designation "Syngestykke" (Singspiel).
